rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991'
rows.abstract: Seeks to strengthen the Sangguniang Kabataan by EXPANDING the definition of youth to INCLUDE all persons who are from fifteen (15) to THRITY (30) years of age. Provides, likewise, the following --- "ALL SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN MEMBERS SHALL BE ENTITLEDTO A PER DIEM OF ONE THOUSAND (P1,000.00) PESOS FOR EACH MEETING OF THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ACTUALLY ATTENDED: PROVIDED, THAT, THE PER DIEM DUE TO EACH SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN MEMBER SHALL NOT EXCEED FOUR THOUSAND (P4,000.00) PESOS PER MONTH."

rows.title_full: AN ACT SEEKING TO IMPROVE CHILD PROTECTION AGAINST ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7610, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7658, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'SPECIAL PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AGAINST CHILD ABUSE, EXPLOITATION AND DISCRIMINATION ACT,' APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Five (5) years after its passage, Republic Act No. 7610, otherwise known as the "Special Protection of Children Against child Abuse, Exploitation and Discrimination Act," is still celberated for its valuable contribution to the cause of children's rights and welfare. Child-carers everywjere have hailed R.A. 7610 as a landmark piece of legislation in the area of child rights advocacy. However, even with its amendment by R.A. 7658, social workers, and other child care-givers still sawvarious areas where R.A. 7610 could be improved. This bill seeks to address indentified problems in those areas. Contains the following features --- (1) Bans and penalized the employment of all children in all forms of hazardous occupations; (2) Defiines "HAZARDOUS OCCUPATION" as used in this Act; (3) Mandates the creation of a CENTRAL DATA BANK to monitor child abuse cases; (4) Expands the meaning of "CHILD TRAFFICKING"; and (4) INCREASES penalties under RA 7610, Providing for Stronger Deterren
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 1997-09-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING METROPOLITAN TRIAL COURTS, MUNICIPAL TRIAL COURTS, MUNICIPAL CIRCUIT TRIAL COURTS AND REGIONAL TRIAL COURTS FROM TAKING COGNIZANCE OF AND DECIDING INCLUSION AND EXCLUSION CASES WITHIN SIXTY (60) DAYS BEFORE ELECTION DAY, AMENDINGFOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT 8189
rows.abstract: Rationale: Despite the admonition by the Honorable Supreme Court to some lower court judges, experiences and records of the Commission on Elections showed that inclusion and exclusion cases have been decided involving not only hundreds and thousandsof voters but also that the decisions were rendered even on election day.  The judiciary was, in effect, utilized as a political tool of unscrupulous politicans. Mandates the following ---" SECTION 3. The decision or roder of the courts in inclusionor exclusion cases received by the Board of Election Inspectors or the Election Officer within the prohibited period of sixty (60) days before elction day shall be null and void. The Election Officer of the City or Municipality affected and the Boarrd of Election Inspectors of the precinct concerned shall not implement the said court decision or order." "SECTION 4. Violation of this Act shall constitute an election offense punsihable udner the Omnibus Election Code (BP 881) as amended by R.A. 8

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF TEMPORARY SHELTERS FOR CHILDREN IN ESPECIALLY DIFFICULT CIRCUMSTANCES IN PROVINCES AND CITIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Notwitstanding the welcome proliferation of NGOs concerned with the welfare and protection of children, there is still a need for more shelters for child abuse victims. While the combined capacities of all child-caring institutions--- both government and NGO run throughout the country only amount to about 12,000, there are about 2.9 million children in especially difficult circumstances, who need such shelters. Even if we assume, that centers are serving twice as much clients as their capacity allows them to, it means that we are serving less than one percent (1%) of those in need of shelter. "Temporary Shleters for Chidlren in Especially Difficult Circumstances Act of 1997" >Defines the term "CHILDREN IN ESPECIALLY DIFFICULT CIIRCUMSTANCES" --- refers to those below 18 years of age who are victims of prostitution and sexual abuse, differently abled, child workers, young offenders, in situations of armed conflict, young victims of natural disasters and calamities, HIV-posit

rows.abstract: Rationale: It is a fact that the local insurance industry is heavily taxed. This has affected the growth of the industry, since the high imposition on insurance premiums has prevented the insuring public from procuring sufficient insurance coveragesfor their properties. LIkewise, this has slowed doen the growth of the economy since a significant amount of losses are not indemnified by insurance. Amends Section 103 of the National Internal Revenue Code to read as follows: "SEC. 103. Exempt Transactions. - The following shall be exempt from value added tax: > x x x > "(u) NON-LIFE INSURANCE COMPANIES, INCLUDING THEIR CROP INSURANCES, AND SURETY, FIDELITY, INDEMNITY AND BONDING COMPANIES."

rows.abstract: Rationale: Our own military establishment has been totally dependent on acquiring or procuring war instruments for use by Filipino combatants in actual operations and on regular training from highly-industri alized nations which are of superior qualities. > A few of these weapons were re-made and adjsuted to suit the local field situations, fully-tested and effective in every encounter, but, this has just reached the limited point of innovation by the AFP logistics services. There is thereforea strong opportunity that exists in mass production of varying qualities of weapons and armaments with the seal of Filipino craftsmanship. "Weapons and Armaments Development Act of 1997" States that the "Armed Forces of the Philippines ... shall endeeavor to develop NEW types of weapons and armaments, including particular accessories ... of high quality ..., technologically advanced as possible, WHOLLY ADAPTABLE to the Filipino culture, as a use of UPGRADING its present inventory and stockpile."

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A PROGRAM OF EDUCATION DESIGNED TO HELP ALL MEMBERS OF THE COMMUNITY OF AN EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTION AVOID INVOLVEMENT WITH ILLEGAL DRUGS
rows.abstract: "The Drug Abuse Prevention Program in Educational Institutions Act of 1997" Declares the following --- "SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy.  It is the policy of the State to promote the health and well-being of the people and rear the youth for nation building.  To this end, it is necessary to provide a program of education on the detrimental effects of the use of illegal drugs designed to help all members of the community of an educational institution avoid involvement with illegal drugs." >The educational program shall emphasize the following subjects: (1) the incompatibility of the use or sale of illegal drugs with the goals of the institution; (2) the legal consequences of involvement with illegal drugs; (3) the medical implications of theuse of illegal drugs; and (4) the ways in which illegal drugs jeopardize the individual's present accomplishments and future opportunities.

rows.abstract: Rationale: "Lead is a silvery gray metal that is toxic in every known form..., lead is hazardous to health even at exceedingly low levels. Children are particularly vulnerable. Concentration of this in body tissues results in fatigue, weakness, lethargy, insomnia, brain damage and muscular paralysis." Penalizes violation of this Act --- "SEC. 3. rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT TO ADDRESS THE NATIONAL WATER CRISIS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Declaration of Policy - The State recognizes the existence of a national water crisis. It is hereby declared the policy of the State to adopt urgent and effective measures to address the antional water crisis, as well as measures for thelong-term sustainable management of scarce water resources.  To achieve this purpose, the utilization and development of water resources must be rationalized and optimized through an integrated approach to planning, development and regulation of thewater sector." Proposes the creation of the WATER RESOURCES AUTHORITY OF THE PHILIPPINES which shall facilitate the preparation, integration, coordination, and supervision of all plans, programs, projects, and activities of the government relative too water exploration, utilization, distribution and conservation.

With the proposed bill every student would have second thoughts before using illegal drugs. With this measure, there is created a fear of detection or discovery if they will be required to udnergo drug test before they are admitted to the schools. > Provides for the following --- "SEC. 2.
